key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse materials design into latent-space optimization by using a generative decoder as a validity prior and physics-informed search to find microstructures that better match target properties.
engineering_relevance: This enables more practical design of magnesium alloy microstructures by reducing dependence on costly simulator evaluations and improving feasibility in a hard-to-encode design space.
method: Encode EBSD-derived microstructure/texture images into a compact latent space with a Vision Transformer.
Decode candidates with latent diffusion / diffusion transformer / rectified-flow transformer models to enforce validity.
Optimize the latent variables with MERIDIAN, combining deep-kernel GP uncertainty, failure-aware feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On about 80,000 EBSD-derived samples, the ViT-FMDiT decoder achieved strong reconstruction quality (FID 27.86, MS-SSIM 0.178), and with MERIDIAN under a 160-simulation budget it reduced relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the learned decoder and simulator fidelity, so generalization to new material systems or different solver settings may require retraining and careful validation.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
